# Docs and CI checks

Owned by the docs package. Run them with:

```sh
node --test --test-concurrency=1 ".github/checks/*.test.ts"
npx tsc --noEmit -p .github/checks
```

The `docs` job of `.github/workflows/checks.yml` runs both. `npm run test:docs` runs the tests.

| File | Checks |
|---|---|
| `docs-rules.ts`, `docs.test.ts` | Every current published page under `docs/` links only to what the docs site can serve: the site is built from `docs/` alone, so a file outside it is linked by its absolute GitHub URL on `main`, and that file must exist in this tree. The vocabulary tables of the generic-model pages equal `contracts/generated/vocabulary.ts`. The decided and deferred counts of the model's pending items, as the pages state them, equal `contracts/model.json`. Every decision in `docs/hub-r4-progress.md` names its source. All tracked text outside `foundation/` and `references/` is checked for personal machine paths and protected build-name shapes, including code, tests, ops and extensionless configuration. Synthetic path exceptions are explicit and restricted to named test files or an exact third-party source path pinned by its byte digest. |
| `test-summary.ts`, `test-summary.test.ts` | Reads what `node --test` printed and writes the counts and every skipped test or suite to the job summary. It fails when no test ran, when one failed or was cancelled, or when the run printed no summary: `node --test` itself succeeds when its pattern matches no file. |
| `test-timings.ts`, `test-timings.test.ts` | Reads the junit report that a test job's runner wrote (`JUNIT_REPORT`, `tools/test-report.ts`) and writes the job's slowest test files to the job summary: the seconds of each file's top-level tests and suites, slowest first, so that a file holding up its shard shows and the measured durations that balance the shards can be checked against a run. It never fails a job; a missing report is noted. |
| `workflow.test.ts` | Each test job of `checks.yml` keeps its output and counts it with `test-summary.ts`, also after a failure, and no job reads a secret. No plain YAML scalar in `checks.yml` or `macos.yml` holds a colon followed by a space, which YAML refuses, so the whole workflow would fail to start. The sharded unit and acceptance jobs list every shard once, hand it to the runner, label each summary by shard, and report one status each (`Unit tests`, `Acceptance on a temporary PostgreSQL`) that requires every shard to pass, with no `continue-on-error`. The unit, acceptance and Linux isolation jobs have their runner write a junit report (`JUNIT_REPORT`), list its slowest files with `test-timings.ts` by shard, also after a failure, and keep it for 14 days as an artifact, uploaded by an action pinned by commit. A newer push cancels the running checks of a pull request, never of `main`. Every `regular` unit shard installs the PostgreSQL 18 client from the PostgreSQL apt repository, bounded, checks that `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` report major 18 and puts them first on PATH. The `Linux isolation` jobs run with the other checks on pull requests and pushes to `main` on `ubuntu-24.04`, in complete unit and acceptance shards with one status (`Linux isolation`); each installs bubblewrap and AppArmor with bounded, retried apt calls, loads the policy that `hub/rules/sandbox/linux.ts` generates for the job's own Node with `apparmor_parser -r`, fails before any test when `osIsolationAvailable()` is false, and runs and counts the files selected by `tools/run-guarded-tests.ts linux` with `HUB_SANDBOX_DIAGNOSTICS=1`, so that every unavailable sandbox attempt names its reason in the log. No workflow changes `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`; the isolation log shows the value in effect. `macos.yml` runs on a push to `main`, a schedule and on demand, never for a pull request, in one bounded `macos-15` job that installs `postgresql@18`, fails when sandbox-exec isolation or `/usr/bin/security` is missing, and counts the unit and acceptance files selected by `tools/run-guarded-tests.ts macos` like the other test jobs. |
| `sandbox-guards.ts`, `sandbox-guards.test.ts` | Every tracked `*.test.ts` that imports `callPackFunction` or `callPackFunctionBatch` (from `hub/rules/api.ts` or `hub/rules/sandbox/sandbox.ts`) or `isolatedCommand` (from `hub/rules/sandbox/isolation.ts`) names `sandboxSkip`, `osIsolationAvailable` or `requireOsIsolation: false`, so it skips instead of failing with `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` where sandbox-exec is missing. The check reads imports, not calls: a test that reaches the sandbox only through another module (the run engine, a test harness) is not covered, and a guard anywhere in the file satisfies it. |
| `file-url-paths.ts`, `file-url-paths.test.ts` | No tracked `*.ts`, `*.mjs` or `*.js` outside `foundation/` and `references/` turns `import.meta.url` into a file path with `.pathname`, which percent-encodes non-ASCII characters and so breaks a checkout under such a path; `fileURLToPath()` is used instead. The vendored Asciidoctor port is the one listed exception: it computes its library paths that way but never reads them. |
| `pack-version.ts`, `pack-version.test.ts` | Every tracked `packs/**/pack.json` keeps the manifest digest, and the bytes of each file it lists, from the newest git commit that changed that pack's version. A later change to either one has to change the version in the same tree. The comparison uses git only. |

Limits: pages that open with a historical or superseded banner are records and keep their original links, some of which do not work on the site. The link check does not follow anchors. The machine-path check covers user homes, root-home paths and variable-data paths, plus personal tilde and Windows home forms; generic tool paths and the OS template `~/Library` are allowed. Only http, https, ftp and ftps network URL paths are excluded per match: hosts are normalized with WHATWG URL parsing; localhost and its subdomains, loopback and unspecified IPv4/IPv6 (including mapped local IPv4), query/fragment values, nested file URLs, editor protocols and /@fs paths remain checked. Network URLs may adjoin Chinese prose, full-width punctuation or Markdown delimiters; every non-ASCII character ends the URL token, so following prose cannot carry its exemption over a machine path. Mounted user-home paths and the macOS private variable-data prefix are included; root-home and variable-data matches retain path boundaries so unrelated nested directory names are not mistaken for machine roots. Forward-slash Windows drive paths require a token boundary (route keys and scp-style remote names are not drive letters); backslash paths remain checked when directly attached to command-line switches, and the Users folder may have either case; separators may be forward slashes or literal or escaped backslashes. POSIX directory names remain case-sensitive. The build-name check rejects release and beta names for protected minor lines regardless of case or name family, including branch names without a patch suffix. Existing hits fail the repository checks and must be reported to the integrator, not silently allow-listed. The approved upstream synthetic home example is allowed only at its exact source path and digest; altered bytes, another path, and every other machine path remain checked. Git supplies the file inventory; every tracked regular file is scanned with NULs removed, and symbolic links are checked by their stored target text without being followed. Frozen archives are excluded; a missing tracked path fails instead of being silently skipped.
